clue.text: Arrived with a fortune provided by lottery organisers

parts.note: arrived means came
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with a big win paid out by the people running the lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: Camelot was for many years the company that ran Britain's National Lottery, so the definition is a company name.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot was the operator licensed to run the UK National Lottery.

clue.text: Rather fat, conservative, male partner

parts.note: hubby is an informal word for husband

explanation.surface: A description of a portly Tory husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and rounded, somewhat overweight in a soft way.

clue.text: Man, lover, upset when losing ring in source of spring water

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word lover

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A heartbroken man and his lover, ring returned, at a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when losing ring' takes O out of LOVER to leave LVER; 'upset' shuffles MAN plus LVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Malvern in Worcestershire is famous for its bottled spring water from the Malvern Hills.

clue.text: Most foolish, however you look at it

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, 'least wise' is the most foolish; as one word it is an old adverb meaning at any rate, in any case.

clue.text: Awfully intense blow giving rise to complaint

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly or messily, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ferocious hit that leads to an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful inflammation of the elbow tendons, a medical complaint associated with racket sports.

clue.text: Person with winning ways about to take on damaging type

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
one who damages is a harmer

explanation.surface: A smooth operator about to take on someone dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take on' is only a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attractive and persuasive who wins people over easily.

clue.text: Two coppers, one old, will find something to chew over

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
d stood for an old penny, a copper coin in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Two pennies, one an antique, give you something to ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: The two coppers are a chemical symbol and a coin: d was the old British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Cud is food a cow brings back up to chew again, hence the idiom of chewing the cud.

clue.text: Wine featured in American journal

indicators.note: featured in signals that the word sits inside the clue's letters

explanation.surface: A wine reviewed in an American magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou is a Loire region whose name labels its wines, such as Anjou rosé.

clue.text: Second samba played in African resort

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: a dance played in a new way is rearranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A second samba is performed at an African holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mombasa is a Kenyan coastal city and beach resort on the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Poet struggling to resist

indicators.note: struggling suggests writhing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer fights against something.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina Rossetti and her brother Dante Gabriel were Victorian poets.

clue.text: Forgotten lane under redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment means rebuilding into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neglected little road now being rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' looks like part of the phrase 'under redevelopment' but is fodder; 'redevelopment' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlearned has been put out of the mind, lost from memory.

clue.text: Man's engine originally seized in traffic hold-ups

indicators.note: seized in says one piece is held inside another

parts.note: traffic jams are hold-ups

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word engine

explanation.surface: A man's car engine has seized up in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seized' looks like an engine failure but puts E inside JAMS; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male given name.

clue.text: Happy to dwell in agreeable street

indicators.note: to dwell in means to live within, so the word sits inside the letters of the clue

explanation.surface: Someone content to live on a pleasant road.
explanation.definitionFit: Blest is an old spelling of blessed, meaning fortunate or joyful.

clue.text: One with not a clue about how to prevent disease?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means around or scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who hasn't a clue about stopping illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate, giving a weakened germ so the body builds immunity, is a method of warding off illness.

clue.text: Sort of treatment you'd be expecting to get?

definitions.text: Sort of treatment you'd be expecting to get?

parts.words: Sort of treatment you'd be expecting to get?
parts.note: 'expecting' means pregnant, so the care is that given by a doctor during pregnancy and birth

explanation.definitionFit: Relating to midwifery, the medical care of pregnant women.

clue.text: Remedial treatment for a persistent glower?

definitions.text: Remedial treatment for a persistent glower?

parts.words: Remedial treatment for a persistent glower?
parts.note: a glower is read as one who glows, and to glow is a polite word for sweating

explanation.definitionFit: A product applied to the armpits that stops sweating.

clue.text: New code, perhaps, getting in one drink, to prevent this?

definitions.text: New code, perhaps, getting in one drink, to prevent this?

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one group goes inside the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
rum is a spirit

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word may come in another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh rule of conduct is brought in at the bar to stop unseemly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns CODE into DECO; N plus DECO goes 'in' I plus RUM. The whole clue also defines: a new code stops this bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper, unseemly behaviour, what a dress or conduct code exists to stop.

clue.text: A soldier taking time to support communist promotion

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A soldier takes time to back a Red propaganda drive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'to support' puts PROP beneath A, GI and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, originally from the Soviet agitation and propaganda department.

clue.text: One who'd personally satisfy your appetite for sweetmeats?

definitions.text: One who'd personally satisfy your appetite for sweetmeats?

parts.words: One who'd personally satisfy your appetite for sweetmeats?
parts.note: the 'one' is a person-shaped biscuit, who satisfies a sweet tooth in person by being eaten

explanation.definitionFit: A spiced biscuit baked in a human shape.

clue.text: Write about piece of music -a bit of Holst?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Compose something about a piece of music by Holst.
explanation.walkthrough: Holst's suite The Planets has a movement named after this planet, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: One movement of Gustav Holst's orchestral suite The Planets is named after this outermost planet.

clue.text: Get car rug from vending machine

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: Buy a car blanket from a slot machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An automat is a coin-operated food dispenser, or a cafeteria built of such machines.

clue.text: Robert and Edward prepared vegetables

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister and founder of the police
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Two men got the vegetables ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the skin off potatoes or carrots is a way of getting them ready to cook.

clue.text: Not the position of a woman preparing for marriage?

definitions.text: Not the position of a woman preparing for marriage?

parts.words: Not the position of a woman preparing for marriage?
parts.note: a bride-to-be collects linen in her bottom drawer, so the opposite place is the highest drawer

explanation.walkthrough: A 'bottom drawer' is the British name for a hope chest, the store of linen gathered before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer means of the highest quality or social class.

clue.text: Organised heartless guy with slender limbs

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, so ran means organised

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word guy is removed

explanation.surface: A capable but cruel man who is long and lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes a person or animal that is tall and long-legged with little flesh.

clue.text: Economy that is necessary for attractive girl

parts.note: a cut is an economy, a saving
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Budget savings needed for a pretty girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is an informal word for an endearing or good-looking person.

clue.text: Dissolute character's new place in France

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man

explanation.surface: A rake moves to a new home in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is a city in Normandy, northern France.

clue.text: Charm ally deceptively, secreting tears

indicators.note: deceptively suggests the letters are disguised, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Win a friend over falsely with crocodile tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal means relating to the glands that produce weeping.

clue.text: Boy of exceptional adroitness

indicators.note: of here means made from, so the word is drawn out of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A skilful youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a young male, a youth.

clue.text: Detective, European, seen to be drunk

parts.note: PI is a private investigator, a detective
eyed means looked at, seen

explanation.surface: A European private eye is noticed being tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Bound to catch small coin in hat

indicators.note: to catch means to hold, so one word is taken inside another

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
a mite is a tiny coin, as in the widow's mite

explanation.surface: Someone sure to grab a small coin dropped in a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' is the adjective meaning restricted; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limited is restricted, held within fixed bounds.
